title: Best Wi-Fi Routers and Mesh Systems UK
short: Standalone routers and mesh Wi-Fi systems compared by speed, range and latency, from budget upgrades to whole-home coverage.
intro: A single router suits most flats and smaller homes, while a mesh system's extra nodes fix dead zones in larger or multi-storey homes. This guide compares routers RTINGS has tested on a standardised platform, having bought and tested over 80 routers, spanning budget standalone routers to premium mesh systems.

products.name: Archer BE900
products.best_for: Buyers with a multi-gigabit internet plan and lots of wired devices
products.summary: RTINGS' best-tested Wi-Fi router, with outstanding top speeds, excellent range and superb wired connectivity that suits a home server or desktop PCs on multi-gigabit connections. It's excessive if you don't have 10Gbps devices, and it's physically large.
cons: Overkill without multi-gigabit internet or 10Gbps devices

products.name: Archer BE550
products.best_for: Most households who don't need a multi-gigabit connection
products.summary: RTINGS' mid-range pick, with excellent speeds suitable for multiple people streaming or downloading simultaneously, and all five Ethernet ports rated for 2.5Gbps. Its biggest weakness is 5GHz range, though it supports TP-Link's mesh functionality if you need to expand coverage later.
pros: Excellent speeds for multiple simultaneous users
All five Ethernet ports rated at 2.5Gbps
Easy setup via app or web interface

products.name: Flint 2 (GL-MT6000)
products.best_for: Tinkerers who want deep configurability without a high price
products.summary: RTINGS praised its excellent speeds and impressive range for a large home, but its standout is highly configurable open-source firmware that includes network-wide VPN setup and advanced options like cellular modem failover, all in an approachable interface. It often goes on sale below its list price.
pros: Excellent speeds and range for the price
Built-in VPN and advanced networking options
cons: Priced close to the higher mid-range pick at full price

products.name: Archer AX55
products.best_for: Buyers with an internet plan under 1Gbps
products.summary: RTINGS' budget pick, able to saturate a connection up to 750Mbps at close range and maintain fast speeds up to nearly 100 feet away, suiting most apartments and small-to-medium homes. It's a Wi-Fi 6 router, so you miss out on the 6GHz band if you have newer Wi-Fi 6E or 7 devices.
pros: Strong speed and range for the price
cons: Large homes may still need a mesh system

products.name: Deco 7 Pro BE63
products.best_for: Larger or multi-storey homes with dead zones
products.summary: RTINGS' top mesh system, maintaining high speeds at distances up to 100 feet with compact, easy-to-place nodes. Start with a two-pack and add a unit later if needed. Basic parental controls are included, but device time limits and network-wide antivirus need a HomeShield subscription.
pros: Fast, consistent coverage across large spaces
cons: Advanced parental controls and antivirus need a paid subscription
Full speed benefit needs Wi-Fi 7 devices

products.name: ZenWiFi ET9
products.best_for: Buyers who want strong mesh performance with no subscription
products.summary: RTINGS' pick if the TP-Link Deco is too pricey or you don't have many Wi-Fi 7 devices. Delivers impressive speed and range with notably low latency for a mesh setup, and unlike several rivals, none of its features are locked behind a monthly subscription.
pros: No features locked behind a subscription
Low latency for a mesh system, good for light gaming
Compatible with other ASUS AiMesh routers
cons: Wi-Fi 7 devices won't reach peak speeds
Can cost more than the TP-Link Deco when the latter is on sale

products.best_for: Buyers who want an affordable, easy-to-expand mesh network
products.summary: RTINGS' budget mesh pick, with a beginner-friendly app and solid speeds for connections up to roughly 700Mbps, including multiple 4K streams. Node placement matters more than on pricier systems, as speeds drop noticeably further from the main unit, and many advanced features are paywalled behind an eero Plus subscription.
pros: Built-in Zigbee and Alexa smart-home support
cons: Speeds drop more at satellite nodes than pricier systems
Many features require an eero Plus subscription

guide.q: Do I need a mesh system or will a single router do?
guide.a: A single, well-placed router is enough for most flats and small-to-medium homes. Consider a mesh system if you have a larger or multi-storey home, thick or concrete walls that block signal, or specific rooms with consistently weak Wi-Fi that repositioning the router doesn't fix.

guide.q: Do I need Wi-Fi 7, or is Wi-Fi 6 enough?
guide.a: Wi-Fi 7 only delivers its full speed benefit if your devices also support it, which is still uncommon outside recent flagship phones and laptops. Wi-Fi 6 or 6E routers remain excellent value and are more than fast enough for most households' current devices.

guide.q: How many mesh nodes do I need?
guide.a: As a starting point, a two-pack suits a small-to-medium home, while a larger or multi-storey home may need three or more. Most mesh systems let you buy additional nodes later, so it's reasonable to start smaller and expand if you still have weak-coverage areas.

guide.q: Does a mesh system add noticeable lag for gaming?
guide.a: Each wireless hop between a device and a mesh node can add a little latency, which may be noticeable for competitive online gaming. If gaming performance matters most, use a wired Ethernet connection where possible, or consider a dedicated gaming router instead of a mesh system.
